ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Joana has several sheets of paper with the drawing of a parrot <image1>. She wants to paint only the head, tail and wing of the parrot, red, blue or green, and the head and tail may have the same color, but the wing may not have the same color as the head or tail. How many leaves can she paint, so that there are not two parrots painted the same way?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached images show an outline drawing of a parrot. The visually relevant parts to be colored are the head, the wing, and the tail; no other parts need to be considered. Reasoning: There are 3 available colors: red, blue, and green. The head and tail may have the same color, but the wing cannot have the same color as either the head or the tail. Case 1: The head and tail are the same color. There are 3 choices for their shared color. The wing must be one of the other 2 colors. This gives 3 × 2 = 6 paintings. Case 2: The head and tail are different colors. There are 3 choices for the head and then 2 remaining choices for the tail, giving 3 × 2 = 6 ordered choices. The wing cannot match either, so it must be the only third color. This gives 6 × 1 = 6 paintings. Total: 6 + 6 = 12.
